questions.question: As a beginning rider, what following distance should you keep from the vehicle ahead?

options.text: Keep at least four seconds of distance.
Get as close as possible.
Do not worry about following distance.
Always ride on the left side of the lane so drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least four seconds of distance.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least four seconds of distance behind other vehicles. Increase this distance if road or weather conditions are poor.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Help you avoid hazards on the road.
Give you a way to escape from danger.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid hazards, stay out of other drivers' blind spots, and escape from danger. Your position should discourage other drivers from entering your lane.

questions.question: Why should you place a load low on your motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You cannot see over a high load.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Placing a load too high makes your motorcycle less stable by raising its center of gravity. This can cause balance problems.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce crash risk?

options.text: Use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Ride very close behind other drivers.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, make yourself visible, signal your intentions, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look at least 12 seconds ahead, recognize hazards, and be ready for changing conditions.

questions.question: How much stopping power does the front brake provide?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
About 95 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the roadside.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the roadside.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and go straight. If you must brake, use only the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the roadside, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others see you.
Practice on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic, practice on a quiet road. This helps you adjust to how your motorcycle handles the extra weight.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride in the lane?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: You may lose traction on one or both wheels.
You may stop sooner than expected.
You may damage your tire.
It may take longer to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may lose traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Using too much brake force causes loss of traction, which can lead to a crash.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid an object or uneven surface, you should:

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle is leaning to one side.
Speed up.
Swerve quickly.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle or uneven surface, approach it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as you can. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb some of the impact. Just before hitting it, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front end.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, you should:

options.text: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake of the tire that is flat.
Apply both brakes.
Not use either brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If one tire goes flat and you must brake, gradually apply the brake of the tire that is not flat. Make sure you know which tire is flat before doing this.

questions.question: In a crash, you can reduce serious injury by doing all of the following, except:

options.text: Wear an approved helmet.
Wear face or eye protection.
Wear protective clothing.
Have a windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a windshield.
questions.explanation: You can reduce injury when riding by wearing an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing. A windshield does not provide the same protection as these items.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Danger ahead.
Stop.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders in a group communicate. When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with their palm facing back, all riders in the group should stop.

questions.question: Drivers entering a highway from a ramp on your right may not see your motorcycle. You should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Flash your lights.
Move to the left of your lane so they can share it, if necessary.
Move into another lane, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles entering the highway. Move to a lane farther from the entrance ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give the vehicle room to safely enter the highway.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: The pavement is dry.
The pavement is wet.
You can see through the vehicle ahead of you.
The sun is out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: You need more following distance when it takes longer to stop. Increase your distance if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy and another driver might try to cut in front of you.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, what could happen?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jolt and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may sound.
Your motorcycle may jolt and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jolt and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jolt and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, your motorcycle may jolt and the rear tire may skid. This can cause you to lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting into a lower gear.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Happen at speeds above 35 mph.
Are caused by worn tires.
Happen at night.
Involve riders who are new to their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders who are new to their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders who do not have much experience on their motorcycles.

questions.question: If either tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Roll on the throttle.
Hold the handle grips loosely.
Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to exit the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If one tire goes flat while riding, ease off the throttle and keep a straight course as you slow down. If you must brake, gradually apply the brake of the tire that is not flat. Make sure you know which tire is flat first.

questions.question: Which of the following provides the best protection?

options.text: Sunglasses
Windshield
Goggles
Face shield

questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What should you NOT check during your pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Fluids.
Headlight and taillight.
Turn signals.
Reflectors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil, fluids, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: What should you NOT check before riding?

options.text: Your tire pressure.
The tread depth on your tires.
How shiny your tires are.
The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.correctAnswerText: How shiny your tires are.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tread wear, and the condition of the sidewalls and tread surface.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you assume?

options.text: Other drivers can see your motorcycle easily.
Other drivers cannot see you.
You don't need to worry about being seen.
You should ride aggressively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than cars. They are hard to see. Ride defensively and assume other drivers don't see you.

questions.question: A rider in your group wants to go faster than everyone else. What should the group do?

options.text: Let that rider go ahead and meet at a planned spot later.
Speed up to keep up with that rider.
Have every rider go at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let that rider go ahead and meet at a planned spot later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster, let them go ahead. Plan to meet at a specific location later.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is illegal.
It is turning off the engine to slow down.
It is slowing down by downshifting.
It damages the engine and should be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle. This is called engine braking.
